title: Stage 9, Lesson 1: How does a mortgage actually work?
subtitle: The mechanics behind the largest loan of most people's lives
openingQuestion: You borrow 2 billion for a home at 9% a year over 20 years. In the early years, what does most of the monthly payment go towards?
openingOptions: Mostly principal, with very little interest
Split evenly 50/50 between principal and interest across the whole term
Mostly interest, with very little principal
Entirely interest, with the principal repaid separately at the end
explanation: On an amortising loan, interest is charged on the balance still outstanding - early on the balance is high, so interest takes the larger share of every payment; later the balance falls and the principal share rises. This is why your net worth grows so slowly through the first five years of a mortgage even though you have paid every month.

diagram.label: The principal borrowed at the start
Early on: interest large, principal small
Late on: principal large, interest small

realWorldExample.description: Banks such as Vietcombank and Techcombank typically advertise a promotional rate of 6-8% a year for the first year or two, after which it floats at a base rate plus a margin (usually 3-4%) - the payment can rise substantially once the promotional period ends, which many borrowers have not planned for.

quiz.question: Why do Vietnamese mortgage rates usually "float" after the first year or two of a promotional rate rather than staying fixed for 20 years?
options: So the borrower benefits if rates come down later
The bank passes the interest rate risk to the borrower
Because a long-term fixed rate does not exist anywhere in the Vietnamese market
Because the central bank requires it by regulation
quiz.explanation: Banks fund themselves short (deposits) and lend long (20-30 years). If the lending rate were fixed for 20 years while deposit rates rose, the bank would take the loss. Floating after the promotional period moves that risk onto the borrower.

quiz.question: Someone finds the monthly payment "affordable" at a promotional rate of 7% and borrows the maximum the bank allows. What is the biggest risk here?
options: The floating rate is usually lower than the promotional one
The monthly payment falls as the loan is repaid over time
Once the promotion ends, the floating rate can reach 11-12%
The bank will automatically extend the 7% promotional rate again
quiz.explanation: Borrowing right up to the affordability limit at the opening promotional rate is a common mistake - it leaves no margin of safety when the rate floats up after a year or two, and that is an entirely predictable event rather than an act of God.

quiz.question: You borrow 2 billion at 8% a year. How much interest is charged in the first month?
options: About 13.3 million dong
About 160 million dong
About 8 million dong
It cannot be determined without knowing the loan term
quiz.explanation: Monthly interest = outstanding balance × annual rate ÷ 12 = 2 billion × 8% ÷ 12 ≈ 13.3 million. The term affects the principal portion and the total paid, but not the interest charged in the first month.

quiz.question: Why should affordability not be calculated at the promotional rate?
options: Because the promotion lasts 1-2 years, after which it floats and rises sharply
Because the bank can demand the loan be repaid in full at any time it chooses
Because the promotional rate differs from one bank branch to another
Because the promotional rate only applies to loans under 1 billion
quiz.explanation: The promotional period is the easiest and the shortest phase of the loan. The right test is to compute the payment at the floating rate plus a margin of safety, and only then decide how much to borrow.

quiz.question: You borrow 2 billion over 20 years. After five years of steady payments, roughly how much of the principal has been repaid?
options: About a quarter of the balance, matching the quarter of the term that has passed
About a sixth of the balance, because most of the early payments are interest
About half the balance, because every monthly payment splits evenly between principal and interest
Nearly all of the principal, because banks always collect principal first and interest afterwards
quiz.explanation: Interest is charged on the balance outstanding, and in the early years that balance is almost untouched, so interest takes most of each payment. This is why selling a home after a few years of payments usually returns far less than the total that has been paid in.

keyTakeaways: An amortising loan pays mostly interest early and mostly principal late
Vietnamese mortgage rates are usually promotional for 1-2 years and then float - the payment can rise afterwards
Do not borrow right up to your affordability limit at the opening promotional rate

practicePrompt.question: You take a 2 billion mortgage over 20 years on an amortising schedule. Why is the payment in month 1 mostly interest while the payment in month 240 is mostly principal?
options: On an amortising loan, early payments are mostly interest and late payments are mostly principal
The bank deliberately charges more interest early to book profit sooner, unrelated to the balance still outstanding
The monthly payment changes at random according to a decision the bank makes on its own each year
This is a common calculation error; the interest and principal portions should be equal every month
practicePrompt.explanation: On an amortising loan, early payments are mostly interest and late ones mostly principal. Interest is charged on the outstanding balance, so as that balance falls the interest share falls and the principal share rises over time.

application.title: Compute the payment after the promotion ends
application.message: Take the loan you are actually considering and recompute the monthly payment at the floating rate, usually the 12-month savings rate plus a 3-4% margin. On a 2 billion loan over 20 years, the payment can jump by several million a month the first month of year three.
application.secondary: That figure, not the promotional one from year one, is what you are committing to for the remaining eighteen years.

sections.text: A mortgage is the largest debt most people will ever sign - and very few of them really understand the amortisation behind it.
Why net worth grows so slowly through the first five years

On an amortising loan, interest is charged on the balance still outstanding - early on that balance is high, so interest takes the larger share of every payment, and only as the balance falls does the principal share start to rise. This is why buyers are so often surprised to find their net worth barely moving through the first years despite paying faithfully every month.

items: An amortising loan pays mostly interest early and mostly principal late
Vietnamese mortgage rates are usually promotional for 1-2 years and then float
Do not borrow right up to your affordability limit at the opening promotional rate

sections.title: Each period's interest is charged on the balance outstanding
sections.equation: This month's interest = Outstanding balance × Annual rate ÷ 12

variables.name: Outstanding balance
variables.description: The principal still unpaid at the start of the period - it falls after each payment.

variables.name: Annual rate
variables.description: The rate applying in that period, whether promotional or floating.

example.title: A 2 billion loan over 20 years at 8% a year
example.result: Out of a payment of about 16.7 million, only around 3.4 million repays principal
example.explanation: In the first month nearly 80% of what you pay is interest. It takes years before the principal share overtakes the interest share - which is why after five years of steady payments the balance has usually only fallen by about 15-20%.

sections.text: What happens when the promotion ends

This is the part borrowers most often fail to plan for. After one or two promotional years the rate switches to floating, set as a base rate plus a margin. If the promotional rate was 8% and the floating rate lands around 12%, the monthly payment in the example above rises from roughly 16.7 million to roughly 22 million - over 5 million more a month, for the remaining eighteen years. That number has to be in the plan at signing, not worked out later.

left.label: Affordability at the promotional rate
left.text: "16.7 million a month against an income of 40 million - that works." This calculation is only true for one or two years, precisely the easiest phase of the loan.

right.label: Affordability at the floating rate
right.text: "If it floats to 12-13%, the payment becomes 22-23 million. On 40 million of income that is over half - too tight." This is the calculation that should decide how much you borrow.

sections.text: Four questions to settle before signing the loan

items: How long does the promotional rate last, and what formula applies afterwards - whose base rate, and what margin?
If you repay early, what is the penalty as a percentage of the balance, and for how many years does it apply?
Beyond the interest, what else is there: appraisal fees, notary fees, compulsory loan insurance, annual property insurance?
If the floating rate rises another 4-5 percentage points, what does the payment become, and can the household still manage it?

sections.label: On repaying early
sections.text: Paying extra principal has the strongest effect in the early years, when the balance is still high and each extra dong of principal cuts interest across the whole remaining life of the loan. But weigh it against the early repayment penalty, and remember that money put into a house is very hard to pull back out when you suddenly need it.

lines: Understanding amortisation keeps you from being surprised that the mortgage "has barely gone down" after the first few years.
That is how the loan works, not a sign that you have been paying it wrong.

summary.keyIdea: An amortising loan pays mostly interest early and mostly principal late
summary.commonMistake: Easy to skip: Vietnamese mortgage rates are usually promotional for 1-2 years and then float - the payment can rise afterwards
summary.action: Do not borrow right up to your affordability limit at the opening promotional rate
